Apple's M5 MacBook Pro is here with a brighter display and 24-hour battery life

Published 2026-10-07 17:05 UTC

Apple announced new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops on Wednesday, powered by its M5, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The design is unchanged, but the mini-LED display now reaches 1,600 nits for SDR content outdoors, and Apple claims up to 24 hours of battery life on the 16-inch model.

The M5 chips are built on a third-generation 3-nanometer process. Apple says the GPU is up to 45 percent faster than the M4 generation and each GPU core now has a neural accelerator for on-device AI work. Every model gets three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SD card slot and MagSafe charging.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 starts at $1,599, the same price as last year. Preorders open today and the laptops ship on October 15th. Apple did not refresh the MacBook Air, which it updated in the spring.

In our first hours with the new laptops, the most obvious change is the display. Apple says the mini-LED panel now reaches 1,600 nits for standard content outdoors, and the difference is easy to see next to last year's model. The nano-texture glass option remains available for an extra $150 and does a good job of cutting reflections under office lights.

Apple's battery claim of up to 24 hours applies to video playback on the 16-inch model with the base M5 Pro chip. Web browsing estimates are lower, at around 18 hours, and heavy GPU work drains the battery much faster. We will run our own battery tests for the full review.

Ports are unchanged: three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SD card slot and MagSafe charging. The base 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 starts at $1,599 with 16GB of memory and 512GB of storage, while M5 Max configurations climb well past $4,000. Preorders open today and the laptops ship next week, with in-store availability on the same day.

Apple did not change the design, so owners of recent models will find the same keyboard, trackpad and speakers. The webcam has been upgraded to a 12-megapixel sensor with Center Stage, which keeps you framed during video calls as you move around.
